native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: Across the supplied country-group aggregates, the contemporaneous log-log elasticity of per-capita income to the share of GNI allocated to education (Adjusted Savings: Education Expenditure, % of GNI) is materially more negative in the Lower-Middle-Income aggregate than in Sub-Saharan Africa — and the differential is statistically robust on the only common-support window the data allow. On the headline 2011–2015 panel (5 annual observations per group, pooled N=10, the binding constraint because SSA's per-capita-GNI series is otherwise absent) the LMC elasticity is −2.07 (HAC(2) SE 0.19, t=−11.0) versus an SSA elasticity of −0.34 (HAC SE 0.02, t=−18.6); their Chow-style interaction β_SSA − β_LMC equals +1.73 (HAC(2) SE 0.19, p<0.001), and the first-difference analogue delivers a same-signed gap of +0.27 (one-sided p≈0.029) on the pooled N=8 FD sample. Stated as required comparative metrics: (a) the elasticity difference between SSA and LMC is +1.73 in log-log levels (and +0.27 in first differences) on the common-support panel; (b) the cumulative impulse-response difference is positive in sign — the LMC anchor is firmly negative on a 5-year horizon (cumulative IRF over lags 0–1–3–5 in FD = −0.36 log-points) while the SSA cumulative response cannot be estimated with precision on the same horizon because only n=5 annual observations are available. The LMC full-sample lag profile is negative at lags 0–5 (β range −0.14 to −1.44, individually insignificant) and turns positive and significant at the 10-year lag (+1.13, t=+2.18, p=0.029), suggesting a delayed-payoff channel that the SSA side cannot exhibit in this dataset. Triangulation on SSA's complete enrolment series shows that SSA's contemporaneous response of primary enrolment to a change in EduExp is weakly positive (+0.015, t=+0.54) while LMC's is negative (−0.027, t=−1.59), and at the 5-year lag the primary-enrolment response is positive throughout the pooled sample (+0.019, t=+1.45) — consistent with the broader picture that SSA's annual co-movement between the education share and per-capita income is materially weaker than LMC's. Disclosures preserved: (i) the education indicator is Adjusted Savings: Education Expenditure (% of GNI), a savings-allocation concept, not government expenditure on education (% of total government expenditure); (ii) the income series is GNI per capita (constant 2015 US$), used as a proxy for per-capita GDP; (iii) with only n=5 annual observations for SSA the SSA coefficient is a directional pattern rather than a precise magnitude; (iv) the negative contemporaneous elasticities partly reflect a denominator/composition effect on a %-of-GNI series, so the differential is the most defensible comparative claim; (v) LMC is a proxy for 'developing countries' (it excludes LIC and most SSA), so the contrast is between the LMC group aggregate and the SSA region aggregate.
native_result.WorkflowB: Three-tier pooled/FD/ARDL regression strategy with Newey-West HAC standard errors throughout. Tier 1 (HEADLINE): pooled 2011–2015 common support (n=5 per group, N=10) with Group x lnX interaction (Chow test) in log-log levels and in first differences; the headline comparative claim is the beta_SSA - beta_LMC interaction. Tier 2 (LMC anchor): log-log level regressions at lags 0/1/3/5/10, FD-ARDL(0,1,3,5,10) for cumulative impulse-responses, level regressions with full controls (primary/secondary enrolment, exports growth, labour force), drop 2008–2010 and 5-year block-average robustness. Tier 3 (SSA triangulation): first-difference regressions of primary and secondary enrolment on d ln(EduExp), both pooled with Group interaction and group-specific, plus a 5-year-lagged primary-enrolment channel to confirm the delayed-payoff pattern. All panels adapted to data availability: SSA per-capita GNI exists only 2011–2015; SSA exports and labour-force start 1991; enrolment series are complete in both groups. Output written to results.json.
